messages:
Alice: Heads up — since last night we've seen a steady trickle of small inference pods (0.25-0.5 GPU requests) being evicted during rack drains, and they end up stuck pending for 10-30m after preemption. App-level retries are exploding.
Ben: Which rack/region? any node labels?
Alice: eu-west1-rack-22. Nodes are a mix of a100-40G and a40s. The small pods are most affected; big jobs (1+ GPU) mostly get scheduled elsewhere.
Chao: That screams fragmentation. small pods can't fit into the remaining fractional slots after gang-scheduling / anti-affinity.
Diane: Can you paste a k8s event or pod describe?
Alice: pasted snippet: ```kubectl describe pod inference-xyz```
Events:
  Normal  Scheduled  5m   default-scheduler  Successfully assigned default/inference-xyz to gpu-node-22-3
  Warning NormalPulled  2m  kubelet  Successfully pulled image
  Normal  Preempted  1m  default-scheduler  Preempted by higher priority pod training-abc
  Warning Backoff  30s kubelet  Back-off restarting failed container
```
Ben: Do we have a scheduler profile that prefers packing large jobs first? Might be doing first-fit that leaves 0.25/0.5 slots scattered.
Chao: Our allocator treats each GPU as indivisible 1.0 units. Small requests are allowed but we don't co-locate multiple small pods on the same GPU because of thermal/cgroup concerns. That policy is causing many 0.25 slots to be stranded.
Diane: Also seen node taints for "rack-maintenance=true:NoSchedule" get applied early during partial drains, which fragments capacity across remaining nodes.
OpsBot: Notice: cluster-autoscaler triggered scale-up of gpu-pool-eu-west1 at 03:12 UTC (reason: insufficient cpu, insufficient nvidia.com/gpu).
Alice: Autoscaler added nodes but they land in a different AZ subset of the rack and the scheduler avoids cross-az placement. So ineffective.
Lena: Short-term mitigation: can we relax the anti-affinity policy for small inference pods to prefer co-location? Toggle to soft affinity for <0.5 gpu requests?
Matt: Risk: co-locating small inference pods increases noisy-neighbor risk — but throttling and cgroup limits could mitigate. Worth testing on a canary nodepool.
Chao: Long-term: two complementary fixes: 1) binpacker change to best-fit-decreasing so we place small pods into existing fractional slots, 2) implement a "defragmenter" controller that gently migrates low-priority small pods onto consolidated nodes, then drains underutilized nodes.
Ben: For defragmenter, we need to avoid mass-throttle/evict storms. Add rate-limited cordon+evict with grace periods and prefer pods with safe restart semantics.
Diane: Also propose marking nodes with a label rack-hetero=true when mixed GPU types exist — let scheduler avoid mixing incompatible GPUs by default, reduce shard scattering.
Alice: Immediate runbook items I suggest: 1) disable strict anti-affinity for inference-svc via a quick config flip (canary 50 pods), 2) create a packed-gpu nodepool with explicit tolerance and kubelet-pin for co-located small pods, 3) bump autoscaler policy to prefer adding nodes in the same AZ rack cube.
Lena: I'll open an RFC for the defragmenter + binpacker changes and include perf/regressions checklist.
Matt: I'll provision a canary nodepool (packed-small-gpus) and run 200 small pods for 2 hours, measure tail latency and eviction rate.
OpsBot: Action logged: RFC ticket INF-534 created by Lena. Canary nodepool request by Matt queued under infra-runbook.
Chao: One more caveat — some training jobs pin GPUs with device plugin topology hints; defragmenter must respect pod topologyHints and not force migrations that break affinity.
Alice: Agreed. Also tracking cost impact: right now wasted fractional GPUs ~12% in rack-22 this week, ~0.6% cluster wide. If we consolidate we might reclaim ~40% of that waste.
Ben: OK plan: run canary + monitor for 24h, if tail latency improves and evictions drop >60% then proceed with defragmenter RFC.
Diane: I'll add a dashboard with per-rack fractional utilization, eviction heatmap, and cross-az placement failures.
Lena: Assigned: Lena -> RFC, Matt -> canary + benchmark, Diane -> dashboards, Chao -> scheduler perf design.
Alice: Thanks all. Will post follow-up with the canary results here. :thumbsup:
